name: Lance Uggla
current_role: Vice Chairman, General Atlantic; co-founder and head of BeyondNetZero (GA's climate growth fund); Mastercard director
profile: Canadian-born British financier who founded Markit in 2003 to provide independent credit-derivative pricing, merged it with IHS in 2016 and sold IHS Markit to S&P Global for ~$44bn (closed Feb 2022). Since 2022 he has been Vice Chairman of General Atlantic and leads its BeyondNetZero climate-transition growth fund.
interesting_fact: Markit began operating out of a barn north of London, born from his 1990s habit at TD Securities of compiling prices for illiquid credit assets; post-Enron demand for independent pricing turned it into a ~$44bn business.
deep_cut_fact: Son of a sawmill manager from British Columbia, he gave C$34.1m to his alma mater Simon Fraser University in 2020 for scholarships, the largest gift in SFU's history; his family foundation also funds Zamcog, a school for street children in Zambia.
notes: Energy-transition investor angle (BeyondNetZero) fits the podcast well. Best route is via General Atlantic.

name: Mark Burnett
current_role: United States Special Envoy to the United Kingdom (since Jan 2025); co-founder, Lightworkers Media
profile: London-born TV producer who built a fortune from unscripted formats including Survivor, The Apprentice, Shark Tank and The Voice. He ran MGM's TV business (United Artists Media Group, then MGM Worldwide Television chairman 2018-2022) and co-founded faith-media company Lightworkers Media with wife Roma Downey. Since January 2025 he has served as US Special Envoy to the UK, focused on trade, investment and culture.
interesting_fact: After five years in the British Army's Parachute Regiment (including the Falklands), he moved to the US in 1982 and worked as a live-in nanny in Beverly Hills and Malibu while selling T-shirts at Venice Beach for $18 each.
deep_cut_fact: His TV career began with adventure racing: after competing in France's Raid Gauloises in 1991, he bought the format rights and created Eco-Challenge, the multi-day expedition race that became his first TV production.
notes: Currently a US government appointee (Special Envoy to the UK), so outreach likely goes via the US Embassy London press office or his production companies; no verified personal/official contact found. Net worth shared with wife Roma Downey.

name: Kit Kemp
current_role: Co-founder and Creative Director, Firmdale Hotels; founder, Kit Kemp Design Studio
profile: British interior designer (MBE) who co-founded Firmdale Hotels with husband Tim Kemp in 1985, starting with the Dorset Square Hotel; the group now runs eleven boutique luxury hotels in London and New York (e.g. Ham Yard, Crosby Street). She designs all the interiors and runs the Kit Kemp Design Studio, a homewares shop and product collaborations.
interesting_fact: She has no formal design training: before hotels she worked for an auctioneer, a Greek shipping company's office and then architect Leszek Nowicki, whose practice is where she met Tim Kemp.
deep_cut_fact: She champions Fine Cell Work, the charity founded by Lady Anne Tree in 1997 that trains prisoners in skilled needlework, commissioning prisoner-made pieces as part of her design collaborations; she has also written four design books, from A Living Space (2012) to Design Secrets (2021).
notes: Wealth shared with husband Tim Kemp. Hospitality/design focus; less obvious fit for energy/data-center themes but strong entrepreneur story.

name: Daniel Allen Gold
current_role: Founder and CEO, QVT Financial LP and QVT Family Office; director of Roivant Sciences and Okeanis Eco Tankers
profile: Hedge-fund manager who ran Deutsche Bank's proprietary trading group and spun it out as QVT Financial in 2003; QVT is a long-time backer of Roivant Sciences and Okeanis Eco Tankers, where he sits on the boards (Roivant compensation committee chair). His wealth reflects QVT's large Roivant stake and other public holdings.
interesting_fact: Before Deutsche Bank he worked at Daiwa Securities and Bear Stearns; he holds an A.B. in Physics from Harvard College.
deep_cut_fact: He was an original board member of rare-earths producer MP Materials when it went public in 2020, and has also sat on the boards of Awilco Drilling and energy-management firm Gridpoint, a natural energy/critical-minerals hook for the podcast.
notes: Low public profile; approach via QVT media contact. Board roles at MP Materials/Gridpoint per 2021 MP proxy; check current status before citing as present-tense.

name: Marie-Hélène Peugeot-Roncoroni
current_role: Peugeot family shareholder; director and deputy CEO (directrice générale déléguée) of Établissements Peugeot Frères (family holding)
profile: Daughter of former Peugeot chairman Pierre Peugeot and a Sciences Po graduate, she began at an accounting firm before working in the family group in corporate finance, industrial relations and HR. She sat on PSA Peugeot Citroën's supervisory board (1999-2014, later vice-chair) and on Peugeot Invest's board until 2022; she holds her stake via EPF, which owns stakes in Stellantis, Forvia and Rothschild & Co.
interesting_fact: The Peugeot family started as a steel foundry in eastern France in 1810 and built its first steam-driven car in 1889; the company merged with Fiat Chrysler in 2021 to form Stellantis.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond the car business she has served on the board of ESSO (ExxonMobil's French subsidiary) and of cleaning/services group ONET, and sits on the board of trustees of the Institut Diderot think tank.
notes: Very private family shareholder with no personal public channels; best route is via Peugeot Invest / EPF. Exact current EPF title per aggregator profiles, not confirmed in an official filing.

name: Oleksandr Yaroslavsky
current_role: President, Development Construction Holding (DCH), Kharkiv, Ukraine
profile: Kharkiv-based Ukrainian businessman, born 1959 in Mariupol, who made his fortune as co-owner of UkrSibbank (sold to BNP Paribas) and then built the DCH group, whose assets have included Kharkiv International Airport, Kharkiv Tractor Plant, FC Metalist and the Kharkiv Palace Hotel. He was a member of the Verkhovna Rada (2002-2006) and Forbes Ukraine ranked him among the country's ten richest in 2016.
interesting_fact: As president of FC Metalist Kharkiv (2005-2012) and owner of Kharkiv airport, he was central to Kharkiv's role as a Euro 2012 host city.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he trained as a food technologist at the Kharkiv academy of public nutrition, served three years in the Soviet army in Hungary, and earned a candidate of technical sciences degree from the Odesa technological institute in 1989.
notes: No working official DCH site or verified personal channels found (dch.com.ua unreachable). Wikipedia article is tagged for poor sourcing and records reputational controversies since 2022; journalist should vet carefully before outreach.

name: Ho Tsz Wan
current_role: Substantial shareholder (via spouse) of Lee & Man Paper Manufacturing (HKEX: 2314); reported director of Lee & Man Construction Holdings
profile: Hong Kong-based wife of Lee Man Bun, CEO and executive director of containerboard maker Lee & Man Paper. Under Hong Kong's SFO she is deemed interested in the 1.30bn shares (30.35%) held by her husband, which is the basis of her Hurun listing shared with him; she is not an executive of the listed company herself.
interesting_fact: Lee & Man Paper's 2025 annual report lists her as a substantial shareholder deemed interested in 30.35% of the company through her husband Lee Man Bun, son of founder Lee Wan Keung.
notes: Private individual with essentially no public profile; aggregator profiles (MarketScreener) say she was a Lee & Man Paper manager 2007-2012, a USC graduate (2003) and INED of Unipact Entertainment, unverified. Better outreach target is husband Lee Man Bun via Lee & Man Paper.

name: Zheng Rong
current_role: Chairwoman and controlling shareholder, Sichuan Yahua Industrial Group (SZSE: 002497)
profile: Born 1953, Zheng Rong (female) led the restructuring of the state-owned Ya'an Chemical Plant into Yahua, which listed in Shenzhen in 2010 and is now both a major civil-explosives maker and a lithium-salt producer for EV batteries. She has chaired the company since 2009 and is its largest shareholder (about 10.2% at end-2025).
interesting_fact: Yahua has grown from a 1952 explosives plant in Ya'an into one of China's notable lithium hydroxide suppliers for battery makers, a direct link to the energy-transition supply chain.
deep_cut_fact: She joined the Ya'an Chemical Plant in 1971 as a workshop worker and worked her way up through deputy chief accountant and deputy director to factory director before leading the 2001 privatization; she is a senior economist and a Sichuan Province Model Worker.
notes: Zheng Rong is a woman (aged 72 per 2025 report). Lithium angle fits energy podcast; route via board secretary office in Chengdu.

name: Zhang Wenrong
profile: Listed on Hurun China Rich Lists 2007-2021 with wealth attributed to 'Yalong' (cable and real estate). Searches in English and Chinese found no reliable public source linking a 张文荣 to a Yalong (亚龙) cable/property group, so identity and current role could not be confirmed.
notes: Could not identify the company (Yalong is unlisted / ambiguous). Needs the full company name or province to research further; likely a very low-profile private-company owner.

name: Quan Qiuhong
current_role: Chairwoman, controlling shareholder and founder, BGT Group (倍杰特, SZSE: 300774)
profile: Born 1970, Quan Qiuhong (female) founded Beijing BGT International Environmental Technology in 2004 after a decade in water-treatment sales and management in Zhengzhou; BGT listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext and specialises in industrial water treatment and zero-discharge reuse of high-salinity wastewater. The company has since expanded into salt-lake lithium extraction and mineral development.
interesting_fact: BGT's core technology recovers resources from high-salt industrial wastewater (e.g. from coal-chemical plants), and it has pivoted that know-how into salt-lake lithium extraction, an energy-transition angle.
deep_cut_fact: She started out in 1995 as the Central China sales agent for Peninsula (半岛) Water Treatment, then became deputy GM (Hong Kong side representative) of its Zhengzhou JV and ran Zhengzhou Dahe Water Treatment Equipment before founding BGT in 2004.
notes: Hurun's 'BGT' = 倍杰特 (identified via cninfo filings). Water/lithium angle relevant to energy and data-center cooling topics. Route via company board office.

name: Zhang Zhimin
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Shenzhen T&S Communications (太辰光, SZSE: 300570)
profile: Born 1951, Zhang Zhimin has chaired Shenzhen-based T&S Communications since December 2000. T&S makes passive optical components, notably high-density MTP/MPO fibre connectors and fibre flex circuits used in hyperscale data centres, and its value has surged with AI computing build-outs; he shares the Hurun listing with his wife Cai Bo.
interesting_fact: T&S's high-density MTP/MPO fibre connectors are widely used in large data centres worldwide, making it a direct beneficiary of the AI data-center boom.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in 1984 as an interpreter and later head of sales at China-Japan (Shenzhen) Leasing, one of Shenzhen's early Sino-foreign ventures, before he ran Shenzhen Zhonghe Optical and moved into fibre optics.
notes: Excellent fit for a data-center podcast (optical interconnect supplier). His board term ran to Sept 2026 per the 2025 annual report; confirm re-election.

name: Zheng Weihe
current_role: Founding partner and Chairman, Cowin Capital (同创伟业), Shenzhen
profile: Born 1966 and holding a Nankai University law master's, Zheng Weihe co-founded Shenzhen Cowin Capital with his wife Huang Li on 26 June 2000, one of China's first professional venture-capital firms. Cowin listed on the NEEQ (832793) in 2015, manages over RMB 35bn and says it has invested in 800+ companies and helped 130 go public; its focus is hard tech, healthcare and the digital economy.
interesting_fact: Cowin claims more than 130 IPOs from 800+ portfolio companies in 26 years, built on an 'industry-chain' strategy of hunting hidden champions in emerging industries.
deep_cut_fact: At a 2023 VC conference he summed up Cowin's playbook as 守株待兔 ('waiting by the tree stump for the rabbit') - building a circle of competence and safety margin - and urged investors to 'seize the AI high ground', naming hard tech, health and digital economy as Cowin's main tracks.
notes: Wealth shared with wife and co-founder Huang Li. Active conference speaker in China VC circles; route via Cowin Shenzhen office.

name: Ke Longtu
current_role: Shareholder (12.5% of Keboda Holdings) and party acting in concert with the controllers of Keboda Technology (科博达, SSE: 603786)
profile: Ke Longtu is the daughter of Keboda co-controller Ke Binghua and holds 12.5% of Keboda Holdings, the parent of Shanghai-listed automotive electronics maker Keboda Technology (lighting control, motor control and EV electronics for VW, Audi and others). Since 2023 she has been formally designated a concert party of the controlling Ke family; she holds no executive role in the listed company.
interesting_fact: Keboda is controlled by brothers Ke Guihua (chairman/president) and Ke Binghua; in 2023 the family extended its concert-party arrangement to the next generation, Ke Lei and Ke Longtu.
notes: Next-generation family shareholder with no public profile; wealth shared with father Ke Binghua. Better outreach target is chairman Ke Guihua via Keboda's board office.

name: Xiong Xianzhong
profile: Appeared on Hurun China (2009-2021) and Hurun Global (2015-2018) lists with wealth attributed to 'Hongkelong' (retail and real estate). No reliable public source was found describing him or the company; Hongkelong may be the Jiangxi retailer 洪客隆, but this could not be confirmed.
notes: Identity unverified (private company; Baidu Baike blocked, web search returned nothing). A person of this name appears in 2025 Changyuan Group (600525) filings as a plaintiff in a securities case; not confirmed to be the same person and not used.

name: Yang Lu
current_role: Minority shareholder of Shanghai Qufeng International Trading (former controlling shareholder of Shanghai New Culture Media); no known executive role
profile: Yang Lu (female) appeared on the 2017 Hurun China list alongside Yang Zhenhua, founder and controller of Shanghai New Culture Media Group (300336.SZ), a film/TV and outdoor-advertising company. In 2017 she acquired 8.33% of Qufeng International, the company's controlling shareholder, with Yang Zhenhua holding 91.67%. New Culture was delisted from Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2023.
notes: Very low public profile; family relationship to Yang Zhenhua not stated in filings. The underlying listed company was delisted in 2023, so the Hurun wealth figure is likely stale. Shareholding source: New Culture 2017 annual report http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2018-04-23/1204679662.PDF

name: Liu Shui
current_role: Founder and former chairman/controller of Shenzhen Techand Ecology (now CECEP Techand, 300197.SZ); no current listed-company role
profile: Born 1969 in Meizhou, Guangdong, Liu Shui studied physical geography at Peking University, worked in turf/lawn-engineering firms, and in 2001 co-founded Techand Ecology, which grew into a major Chinese ecological restoration and landscaping contractor listed on ChiNext in 2011. Control later passed to state-owned China Energy Conservation and Environmental Protection Group (CECEP), and the company is now chaired by He Liang.
interesting_fact: He picked the company name Techand (铁汉, 'iron man') himself and coined its slogan 铮铮铁汉，顶天立地 ('an iron man, standing tall between heaven and earth').
deep_cut_fact: A Hakka from Meizhou who attended the city's Dongshan Middle School, he was named from a family phrase: his parents named their four children Liu Xi, Liu Shui, Liu Chang and Liu Qing after 溪水长情 ('streams flow with lasting affection').
notes: No longer controls the company. Per a May 2026 report the Shenzhen Stock Exchange barred him for three years from serving as a listed-company director over related-party fund occupation (https://caifuhao.eastmoney.com/news/20260507100153176423950); Hurun wealth figure is likely stale. Approach with caution.

name: Liu Chunhai
current_role: Retired; former Vice President of Inner Mongolia Yili Industrial Group (600887.SH), still a top-10 individual shareholder
profile: Liu Chunhai is a long-time Yili executive who served as a director and vice president of China's largest dairy company from 2007 until retiring at the statutory age in April 2023. His wealth comes from his Yili shareholding (about 85 million shares, ~1.3%, at end-2023), built up partly through the company's equity-incentive plans.
interesting_fact: He was one of the largest individual shareholders of Yili, holding roughly 85 million shares (about 1.34%) at end-2023, a stake worth well over RMB 2bn.
notes: Retired corporate executive with no public profile; filings give only a two-line bio. Any contact would go via Yili's investor relations office.
